§1 — The tape model has never met a measurement

quench-detection-converter-pickup §4 built the co-wound tape as a winding element. coil_windings.co_wound_tape carries a second conductor that follows a sectioned winding turn by turn, coupled to it almost perfectly in inductance and capacitively through the turn insulation. That section formed the CS comparisons QI1 − QI3 and QI2 − QI4 that R3M9BQ v3.0 defines and drove them with CS1's switched ripple. At the converged solve, the pickup through either front end stays well under the 50 mV noise target.

That result rests on a model no measurement has checked. The tape's strip width, its insulation thicknesses and its place in the turn are not in IDM, so §4 stated them as assumptions and ran both ends. The comparison transfer also moved by about a factor of fifteen between a one-section-per-pancake solve and the converged one. A model that sensitive to resolution and to unsourced geometry needs a measurement before its result is relied on.

The only measured converter-to-tape transfers held anywhere are the TF cold tests. tf-cold-test-validation §10 measured, on TF07 and TF17 at the magnet cold test bench:

  • the per-double-pancake transfer from the converter to the co-wound tape, raw and compensated, per converter line;
  • the rejection, compensated over raw, central against edge pancakes;
  • the common-mode split;
  • a near-1 Hz ramp rejection.

That plan measures and builds no tape element, and it names the element's single owner as quench-detection-converter-pickup §4. The comparison needs a sectioned TF winding, and none exists in coil_windings, which covers the PF and CS coils. Building it is a modelling job of its own, because the TF winding sits in the grooves of radial plates and its capacitive paths differ from a PF or CS pancake's. The lead decided on 21 October 2026 to build it here, in a plan of its own, rather than inside quench §4.

§2 — A sectioned TF winding

Add the TF coil to coil_windings as a sectioned winding the existing node solve can take, beside the PF and CS layouts. Take each value from IDM, through the coordinator, who looks it up and passes it in the brief:

  • the turn count;
  • the double-pancake structure;
  • the radial-plate geometry;
  • the insulation between conductor and plate, between plates, and from the plates to the case.

Where IDM is silent, state the assumption and run both ends of its range. The capacitive paths are conductor to radial plate across the turn insulation, plate to plate, and plate to case across the ground insulation. No TF conductor geometry exists in the repository. Every machine-description reader opens pf_active only (frequency_response_prediction.machine_geometries, scripts/iter/coil_windings.py, converter_filter_study), and coil_self_inductance indexes PF coils. Two sources carry the TF coil's self-inductance: the project's register src/power_convertor/registers/iter_supplies.json (supplies.TF.coil_self_inductance_h, 0.349 H from the SRD, with a string inductance of 17.7 H), and 3PAJ8K v1.3's static FEA value, 0.34641 H. They differ by 0.7 %. State which the winding uses, set the other beside it, and partition the coil inductance between the double pancakes as a stated assumption, at both coupling ends.

Form the plate-to-plate and plate-to-case capacitances through coil_windings.capacitance_budget and _plate, extending them with a TF stack rather than writing a parallel estimator. The section adds a TF layout record, a TF insulation stack, a SECTIONED_KINDS member and a SECTION_SPLIT entry. It retires nothing, because no TF winding exists to replace, and its record says so.

Derive the converged section count by the rule the PF coils use: the three lowest winding modes within 3 % of the turn-resolved build.

Done when the TF winding builds at turn resolution and at its converged count, and the record states:

  • the converged count;
  • the three lowest modes at both resolutions;
  • the low-frequency terminal-to-ground capacitance, beside any measured value tf-cold-test-validation holds.

Negative control: removing the plate-to-case capacitance drops the terminal-to-ground capacitance to the conductor-to-plate path alone, which the record states.

§3 — The TF tape against TF07 and TF17

Build the co-wound tape's TF instance with coil_windings.co_wound_tape on §2's winding at its converged count. The element carries its grouped sums at any solve resolution (merged a4d97247). quench-detection-converter-pickup §4 replaced the tape's static capacitive divider with a distributed RC line along the strip (TapeStrip, strip_line_response) before it closed. co_wound_tape reaches pancake_section_bounds, which accepts only PANCAKE_SECTION_KINDS (“hexapancake”, “pancake”), so extend it to the TF layout's section kind rather than relabelling the TF winding. TF07 and TF17's near-1 Hz rejection is exactly the measurement that tells those two models apart.

The TF tape's stack is stated, not looked up, wherever the TF drawings are silent. Each assumption takes a low and a high end, both run:

  • the gap and permittivity between the tape and the conductor;
  • the gap and permittivity between the tape and the radial plate's groove wall, which the TF tape faces where the CS tape faces the next turn;
  • the inductive coupling to the turn;
  • the strip's series resistance per pancake.

Widen TapeInsulation's defaults to carry a per-coil stack, CS and TF, rather than adding a parallel TF_TAPE_* constant family. The CS ranges, CS_TAPE_* in coil_windings, are the starting priors. The CS module site acceptance test, 3JUPSH v3.1 (PDF 20–22), reads 4–5 kΩ from each co-wound-tape tap to the conductor. That is a CS value, not a TF one, so it bounds the TF strip only by analogy. A TF reading, if tf-cold-test-validation holds one, takes its place. Each of these is an assumption the comparison below can constrain.

Form the per-double-pancake tape signals as the cold test wired them, and drive them with the measured converter line voltages. Read those lines, keyed by frequency on one time reference, through their existing owner: the store root cold_test_data.DEFAULT_ROOT and the loader scripts/mctb/current_controllers.load_transfers, not by path. Build the TF instance through quench_detection.cs_tape_pickup, generalised beyond its CS-only gate, rather than a fork. Compare with the measured quantities as scripts/mctb/quench_detection.py computes them: transfer_statistics, rejection_rows, ramp_rejection and common_mode_split. Compare against the measured per-DP transfer and the measured rejection.

The near-1 Hz ramp rejection is a lower bound set by the archive step: 279 on TF07 and 177 on TF17. A model rejection above it is consistent with the measurement, not refuted by it.

Where the model misses a measurement, report by how much, at which double pancake and which line. Name the stated tape assumption the measurement constrains, and the range of that assumption the measurement admits. Do not tune the tape to the measurement: a constrained range is the finding, and carrying it to the CS result is §4's.

Done when the record tabulates, for TF07 and TF17, each double pancake's modelled and measured transfer and rejection at every measured line. It also gives the deviation and names the constrained assumption with its admitted range. A figure draws the comparison, rendered and inspected.

Negative control: a tape with no capacitance to the winding, coupled only inductively at unit coupling, gives a rejection no measurement shows, and the record states that comparison.

§4 — Carry the verdict to the CS result

State what §3's verdict means for the CS tape pickup. quench-detection-converter-pickup closed on 21 October 2026 with the CS result awaiting this validation, so the verdict goes into the CS tape record, docs/research/iter-cs-quench-tape-pickup.html, as a dated note. Where the claims register carries the CS result, it also goes there. Three outcomes are possible:

  • the measurement admits the CS assumptions' range, and the CS result stands as validated;
  • it narrows the range, and the CS pickup is restated on the narrowed range;
  • it excludes the range, and the CS result is reopened.

Done when the CS tape record carries the dated verdict, naming the outcome and the numbers that decide it. Where the claims register carries the CS result, its row is updated to match.

§2 closed (merged caeebf3e). The ITER TF coil builds as a sectioned winding of seven radial plates and 134 turns, with 3PAJ8K's 0.34641 H and a plate capacitance network. It converges at 28 sections, within 2.43 % of the turn-resolved modes. Its terminal-to-ground capacitance is 0.61 µF nominal, with no measured TF value to compare. evidence

Inputs from tf-cold-test-validation's synthesis (docs/research/tf-cold-test-synthesis.html, landed a57aa493), for §3 and §4:

  • Pair comparisons. The cold-test thresholds apply to the pair comparisons DP17, DP26, DP35 and DP42. The worst raw pair is −176 mV against the 30 mV threshold, at TF07 DP42 on the 5 kA flat top. Four of five raw taps are at or past 30 mV, while the tape-compensated pairs hold their margins. That is a validation control for the tape's compensation.
  • Rejection. The tape rejection medians, 279 on TF07 and 177 on TF17, are lower bounds where the compensated residual sits at the archive step. The compensated FDU-opening spike peaks at 48.6 mV on TF07.
  • Coupling constants. The passive-mode posterior gives k2 = 0.792 [0.765, 0.817] and τ2 = 0.506 s [0.484, 0.528]. That contains the 0.80 and 0.49 s that winding_losses carries and that quench-detection-converter-pickup §6 flagged as a material analogy. The coupling secondary therefore stands on a measured TF posterior.
